items.title: 降价30%，Gucci在中国卖不动了
items.summary: Tencent News trade analysis on Gucci's China price cuts (up to 30-40% off classic bags, e.g. GG Marmont small bucket bag falling below 10,000 yuan). Ties the markdown to Kering's H1 2026 results showing Gucci revenue down 9% YoY to 2.76bn euros and Asia-Pacific down 10%, with weak store traffic despite higher average transaction value among remaining buyers. Frames the cuts as part of the 'Rinascimento' turnaround plan.

items.title: 古驰地震：Demna上任、降价40%、关店百间，品牌转向何方？
items.summary: Sina analysis describing Gucci's overhaul as "断臂求生" (sacrificing a limb to survive): Demna's deconstructivist debut (La Famiglia/The Tiger film) reinterpreting Bamboo 1947 and Horsebit loafers, price cuts up to 40% in China, and a store-closure plan (75 closed in 2025, 100 more planned in 2026). Presents a cautious, bifurcated consumer outlook -- heritage buyers advised to seek untouched classics, trend-followers may embrace the experimental direction, investors face uncertainty.

items.title: 古驰突然大降价：最高降40%！经典款跌破万元，还能买吗？
items.summary: Weibo consumer-facing post/thread discussing whether it's worth buying Gucci now that classic styles have dropped below 10,000 yuan after the 40% price cut. Reflects price-sensitive shopper sentiment and skepticism about whether markdowns signal declining brand value versus a genuine buying opportunity.

items.title: 一日连关两店，Gucci在中国"失宠"了吗？
items.summary: Trade/community analysis revisiting why Gucci has fallen out of favor with Chinese consumers, citing Gen Z commentary that its designs are "increasingly boring" and a running joke of "never buy Gucci without a discount." Also notes Gucci underperforms peers like Chanel and Hermes on secondhand/resale value retention.

items.title: 프라다가 열고 뎀나의 구찌가 잇는다… 역대 최대 규모 밀라노 패션위크 온다
items.summary: WWD Korea trade preview of Milan Fashion Week (Sept 22-28, 2026, ~218 shows, ~141,000 expected visitors), calling Demna's Gucci show on September 25 at 2pm one of the week's most anticipated events, alongside Prada's opening show and Moschino's new creative direction. Frames the week as an attempt to revive Italy's fashion sector amid a projected 1.6% 2026 revenue decline.

items.title: 구찌, 2026 가을·겨울 아이웨어 새 시선
items.summary: Korean lifestyle-desk coverage of Gucci's Fall/Winter 2026 eyewear campaign (art direction Riccardo Zanola, photography Mark Seliger), describing portrait-style imagery and double-G/horsebit detail sunglasses and optical frames for men's and women's lines. Standard brand activation coverage.

items.title: "JIN=초고속 매진 단 하나의 기폭제" 방탄소년단 진 구찌 캠페인 품절 집중 조명
items.summary: Korean entertainment-desk report citing French magazine Paris Select Book on BTS member Jin's Gucci Primavera campaign: the $9,900 black leather rider jacket he wore sold out online within a day of the campaign's August 25 release, framed as evidence of a measurable "Jin Effect" on sales. Notes Jin has been Gucci's global ambassador since 2024 and is positioned as the face of the brand's Demna-era creative transition.

items.title: 不振のグッチ｢日本だけが好調｣その"カラクリ"
items.summary: Japanese business-press analysis contrasting Gucci's steep declines in Japan (fashion & leather goods down ~24% YoY in the region even as company-wide category sales fell ~3%) against the fact that Japan is the only market where all three of Kering's core brands (Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta) are simultaneously posting growth. Examines the structural reasons -- repeated price hikes elsewhere driving inbound/tourist demand to Japan -- behind this divergence.

items.title: Gucci cuts prices, but will Chinese shoppers return?
items.summary: Jing Daily (T2 China-luxury trade press) analysis of Gucci's China price cuts, reporting that cautious Chinese consumers are questioning whether luxury goods still justify their pricing, adopting a wait-and-see attitude in hopes of further reductions, and in some cases favoring gold over apparel/leather goods as a value store. Frames the cuts as a high-stakes test of whether discounting can rebuild demand without further eroding brand desirability.
